#uranium #copper #silver #gold

⚡ THE DAILY METALS PULSE — 1 SEPTEMBER 2026 ⚡

Four metals. One pulse. No noise.

The macro squeeze tightened overnight.

US 10-year yields have reached 4.78%, while Brent has climbed above $91. Higher energy prices strengthen the inflation argument, and markets now assign roughly a 66% probability to a September Fed hike.

But China just delivered a stronger industrial signal.

☢️ URANIUM

Numerco’s physical U₃O₈ spot assessment remains around $89.38/lb.

That is an OTC uranium-market indicator, not the price of an ETF, trust or uranium miner.

The new sector development is Westinghouse. Its planned IPO could reportedly value the company at $15–20 billion. Cameco owns 49%.

This does not immediately change uranium spot demand, but it would give the nuclear revival a major public-market benchmark and potentially more capital for reactor deployment.

🟠 COPPER

Copper has strengthened to around $6.62/lb.

China’s private manufacturing PMI rose from 50.9 to 51.5, beating expectations. Output expanded at its fastest rate in three months, while exports grew at their quickest pace in six months.

Meanwhile, Chilean copper production fell 9.4% year over year in July, reaching its lowest July level since 2011.

Stronger Chinese activity and weaker mine supply are pulling in the same direction. That is why copper is absorbing the jump in global yields better than precious metals.

🥈 SILVER

Silver is holding around $66.5/oz.

Its industrial side is benefiting from stronger manufacturing across China and much of Asia. Its monetary side is facing a 4.78% US 10-year yield and increasingly aggressive Fed expectations.

For now, those forces are cancelling each other out. Silver is consolidating, not collapsing.

🥇 GOLD

Gold has slipped approximately 0.4% to $4,429/oz.

Even escalating Middle East tensions and Brent above $91 have not been enough to overpower higher yields and rate-hike expectations.

That is revealing. The market currently fears the monetary response to the energy shock more than the geopolitical shock itself.

US employment data will now decide whether that calculation holds.

Uranium is quiet.
Copper has both demand and supply support.
Silver is caught between two identities.
Gold is fighting the bond market.

Like Buddhism says, the market of last year is not the market we have today. It’s not completely different, but it’s not the same either.

That’s also why strategies used to work for much longer periods 10 or 20 years ago. Today, the speed of change in markets is substantially faster, and the variables that move markets change with it. The past can be a reference point, but it can’t be treated as a fixed formula for the future.

That’s why backtesting that looks back three, five, or ten years is absolutely meaningless. You’re testing a strategy against a market that no longer exists.

𝗛𝗢𝗪 𝗧𝗢 𝗛𝗘𝗗𝗚𝗘 𝗬𝗢𝗨𝗥 𝗣𝗢𝗥𝗧𝗙𝗢𝗟𝗜𝗢 𝗥𝗜𝗚𝗛𝗧 𝗡𝗢𝗪?

Before you read this on how I recommend hedging your portfolio in the current environment, first read my previous tweet below it: “What Are You Hedging Against?”

The idea is simple. If your kid rides his bike only inside the house, you probably don’t need to insure it against a total loss. That would be expensive and unnecessary. You insure against the kind of damage that is actually likely to happen.

Same with hedging. First define what you are protecting against. Then build the hedge around that risk.

If everyone is already afraid of a 10% correction and hedge funds have already deleveraged, I struggle to see where the sellers come from for a full 10% drawdown.

But let’s assume they are partially right and we get a correction.

I see four possible outcomes over the next 45 days, into the October 16 expiration:

5% chance: market goes up 5% in the next 45 days

30% chance: The market goes higher. You deleveraged, so you barely participate.

30% chance: The market stays around current levels. Some stocks do well, but because you deleveraged, you probably don’t.

30% chance: We follow the historical pattern and the market corrects, but because everyone is already positioned for it, the drawdown is more like 1% to 7%, not 10%.

5% chance: The market actually falls 10% or more.

Taking that distribution into account, I like a creative hedge/trade on $QQQ into the October 16 expiration:

Buy the 715 put.
Sell 3 puts around 650, roughly 9% lower.
Sell the 750 call, roughly 5% higher.
It’s opened for a $19 credit.

The trade does especially well if the market falls somewhere between roughly 5% and 11%.

The idea is simple: stay exposed to some upside while protecting yourself against the kind of downside I think is actually more likely over the next 45 days.

Earth is just one of about 100 billion planets in our galaxy, which is just one of about two trillion galaxies in the universe. And our lifetimes are only about 1/3,000 of humanity's existence, which itself is only 1/20,000 of the Earth's existence. 

In other words, we are unbelievably tiny and short-lived and no matter what we accomplish, our impact will be insignificant. 

At the same time, we instinctually want to matter and to evolve, and we can matter a tiny bit--and it's all those tiny bits that add up to drive the evolution of the universe. #principleoftheday
